# Shift-SUV {#sec-shift-suv}

**Shift-SUV is a second car family, sport-utility bodies in two rear-end styles, read through DrivAerML's pipeline unchanged so that a model trained on one family can be scored on another. No cross-architecture standing of ISLA exists on it.** The chapter follows the shared layout; its standing section carries the three-protocol table when the dataset's lanes are scored and nothing before. The pose and discretization probes of @sec-invariances are not run on this dataset. Protocol: @sec-protocol.

```{python}
#| label: setup-shift-suv
#| include: false
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean
from matplotlib.colors import TwoSlopeNorm
from matplotlib.collections import LineCollection
PF = RES / "problem_figures_2026-09-22"

def load_problem(name):
    """One representative sample of a dataset, reduced for plotting (results/problem_figures_2026-09-22/)."""
    z = np.load(PF / f"{name}.npz"); meta = json.load(open(PF / f"{name}.json"))
    return {k: z[k] for k in z.files}, meta

SF = RES / "sample_figures_2026-10-02"

def load_samples(name):
    """Several samples of a dataset, reduced for plotting (results/sample_figures_2026-10-02/); per-sample arrays are
    concatenated and cut with the matching ``*_offsets`` array via ``part``."""
    z = np.load(SF / f"{name}.npz"); meta = json.load(open(SF / f"{name}.json"))
    return {k: z[k] for k in z.files}, meta

def part(a, off, i):
    """Rows of the concatenated array ``a`` that belong to sample ``i``."""
    return a[off[i]:off[i + 1]]

def bc_segments(ax, pts, cells, kinds, lw=4.0, zorder=3):
    """Draw line cells colored by boundary-condition kind (keys of palette.BC)."""
    segs = pts[cells][:, :, :2]
    ax.add_collection(LineCollection(segs, colors=[BC[k] for k in kinds], linewidths=lw, capstyle="butt", zorder=zorder))

def field_scatter(ax, xy, v, s=3.0, signed=False, vmin=None, vmax=None):
    if signed:
        lim = max(abs(np.nanmin(v)), abs(np.nanmax(v))) if vmin is None else None
        norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vcenter=0.0, vmin=(-lim if vmin is None else vmin), vmax=(lim if vmax is None else vmax))
        return ax.scatter(xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], c=v, s=s, lw=0, cmap=DIVERGING, norm=norm, rasterized=True)
    return ax.scatter(xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], c=v, s=s, lw=0, cmap=SEQUENTIAL, vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax, rasterized=True)

def small_colorbar(fig, sc, ax, label, **kw):
    cb = fig.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, fraction=0.035, pad=0.02, **kw); cb.outline.set_visible(False); cb.ax.tick_params(labelsize=8)
    cb.set_label(label, fontsize=8.5)
    return cb

def bc_legend(ax, kinds, loc="lower right", extra=()):
    from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
    handles = [Line2D([], [], color=BC[k], lw=4, label=BC_LABEL[k]) for k in kinds] + list(extra)
    ax.legend(handles=handles, loc=loc, fontsize=8, frameon=True, facecolor="white", edgecolor=BASELINE)

# ---- the three-protocol headline table ----
# The three architectures' reference configurations scored on (i) the native validation mesh, (ii) a uniform point cloud of
# the same budget and (iii) every validation case rotated and translated. Read from results/char/<dataset>.json when that
# artifact exists; until it does the cell prints nothing and the native-mesh table above is the headline. Expected schema:
# {"fields": {key: label}, "protocols": {"native": label, "uniform": label, "posed": label}, "isla_arm": name,
#  "arms": {name: {protocol: {field: {"mean": x, "seeds": [...]}}}}}.
def protocol_table(artifact, label, setting):
    p = RES / "char" / artifact
    if not p.exists():
        return
    C = json.load(open(p)); protos = C["protocols"]; fields = C["fields"]; isla = C["arms"][C["isla_arm"]]
    flab = " / ".join(fields.values())
    hdr = "| configuration | " + " | ".join(f"{pl}: {flab}" for pl in protos.values()) + " |\n|---|" + "---|" * len(protos) + "\n"
    rows = []
    for arm, d in C["arms"].items():
        rows.append(f"| {arm} | " + " | ".join(" / ".join(f"{d[pk][f]['mean']:.4f}" for f in fields) for pk in protos) + " |")
        if arm != C["isla_arm"]:
            rows.append(f"| {arm} ÷ ISLA | " + " | ".join(" / ".join(f"{d[pk][f]['mean'] / isla[pk][f]['mean']:.2f}" for f in fields) for pk in protos) + " |")
    print(hdr + "\n".join(rows) + "\n")
    print(f": {setting}: the three architectures at their reference configurations under three scorings of one instrument, the "
          f"native validation mesh, a uniform point cloud at the same budget, and every validation case rotated and translated; "
          f"fields {flab}; seed means, float32. How to read this: a ratio is baseline ÷ ISLA, above one favoring ISLA; the three "
          f"columns share the checkpoint and differ only in how the validation cases are presented. Data: results/char/{artifact}. "
          f"{{#{label}}}")

```

## The problem: two sport-utility families {#sec-shift-suv-problem}

**Shift-SUV is about a thousand sport-utility bodies in each of two rear-end families, estate and fastback, in one far-field condition, with the same reference length and far-field direction as DrivAerML at a lower speed.** The model receives exactly what it receives on DrivAerML: surface cells with positions, outward normals and areas, and the far-field direction. @fig-problem-shift-suv shows one fastback case.

```{python}
#| label: fig-problem-shift-suv
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The SHIFT-SUV zero-shot target, on one fastback case. The vehicle surface
#|   (150,000 of its 5 million cells at their centroids) colored by the
#|   pressure coefficient $C_p = (p - p_\infty) / \tfrac{1}{2}\rho U_\infty^2$,
#|   seen from the side and from above; the black arrow is the far-field
#|   direction $\hat g_1$. What varies per sample is the geometry; the far-field
#|   speed is fixed and lower than DrivAerML's, a covariate shift every model
#|   sees alike since none receives the Reynolds number. What the model
#|   receives is exactly what it receives on DrivAerML (positions, normals,
#|   areas, $\hat g_1$), which is what makes the zero-shot transfer possible.
#|   How to read this: the same color scale as @fig-problem-drivaer, so the
#|   two bodies can be compared by eye. Data:
#|   results/problem_figures_2026-09-22/shift_suv.npz.
#| code-fold: true
S_, Sm = load_problem("shift_suv")
sp, cp = S_["surf_points"], S_["surf_cp"]
norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vcenter=0.0, vmin=-1.5, vmax=1.0)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8, 5.6), sharex=True, gridspec_kw=dict(height_ratios=[1.0, 1.15], hspace=0.15))
ax = axes[0]
depth_scatter(ax, sp[:, [0, 2]], sp[:, 1], cp, s=2.2, cmap=DIVERGING, norm=norm); map_axes(ax)
U = S_["U_inf"]; bb = S_["surf_bbox"]; x0 = bb[0, 0] - 1.9; z0 = 0.5 * (bb[0, 2] + bb[1, 2])
ax.annotate("", xy=(x0 + 1.2, z0), xytext=(x0, z0), arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=INK, lw=2.0))
ax.text(x0 + 0.6, z0 - 0.1, f"far field: $U_\\infty$ = {np.linalg.norm(U):.0f} m/s\nalong $\\hat g_1$", ha="center", va="top", fontsize=8.2, color=INK2)
ax.set_xlim(x0 - 0.2, bb[1, 0] + 0.3)
ax.set_ylabel("z [m]"); ax.set_title(f"side view: $C_p$ on the {Sm['family']} family", fontsize=9.5)
ax = axes[1]
sc = depth_scatter(ax, sp[:, [0, 1]], sp[:, 2], cp, s=2.2, cmap=DIVERGING, norm=norm); map_axes(ax)
ax.set_ylabel("y [m]"); ax.set_xlabel("x [m]"); ax.set_title("top view: $C_p$", fontsize=9.5)
cb = fig.colorbar(sc, ax=axes, fraction=0.025, pad=0.01, extend="min"); cb.set_label("$C_p$ [–]"); cb.outline.set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: para-shift-suv-samples
#| output: asis
Ss_, Ssm = load_samples("shift_suv")
cs = Ssm["cases"]
def _rng(fam, k):
    v = [c[k] for c in cs if c["family"] == fam]; return min(v), max(v)
La, Lb = min(c["length"] for c in cs), max(c["length"] for c in cs); Wa, Wb = min(c["width"] for c in cs), max(c["width"] for c in cs)
print(f"@fig-shift-suv-samples shows three validation bodies of each family, the first, the middle and the last of each family's validation list. "
      f"The morphs keep the footprint (length {La:.2f} to {Lb:.2f} m, width {Wa:.2f} to {Wb:.2f} m across the six) and differ in height: "
      f"the height runs from {_rng('estate', 'height')[0]:.2f} to {_rng('estate', 'height')[1]:.2f} m among the estates shown and from "
      f"{_rng('fastback', 'height')[0]:.2f} to {_rng('fastback', 'height')[1]:.2f} m among the fastbacks; the far field is "
      f"{np.linalg.norm(cs[0]['U_inf']):.0f} m/s along $\\hat g_1$ in every case.")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-shift-suv-samples
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Six SHIFT-SUV validation bodies, three estates (top row) and three
#|   fastbacks (bottom row), seen from the side and colored by the surface
#|   pressure coefficient $C_p$ on one shared scale (60,000 of each body's cells
#|   at their centroids); the body length, width and height are printed per
#|   panel and the black arrow is the far-field direction $\hat g_1$, the same
#|   for every body. How to read this: within a row the bodies are morphs of
#|   one family, between the rows the rear end changes class; the scale is the
#|   one of @fig-problem-shift-suv and @fig-problem-drivaer so the three
#|   car sets can be compared by eye; colors are the reference CFD field, not
#|   predictions. Data: results/sample_figures_2026-10-02/shift_suv.npz.
#| code-fold: true
Ss_, Ssm = load_samples("shift_suv")
cs = Ssm["cases"]; so = Ss_["surf_offsets"]
norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vcenter=0.0, vmin=-1.5, vmax=1.0)
xlim = (min(c["bbox"][0][0] for c in cs) - 0.3, max(c["bbox"][1][0] for c in cs) + 0.3)
zlim = (min(c["bbox"][0][2] for c in cs) - 0.1, max(c["bbox"][1][2] for c in cs) + 0.6)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(8, 4.4), sharex=True, sharey=True, gridspec_kw=dict(hspace=0.3, wspace=0.05))
for i, c in enumerate(cs):
    ax = axes[i // 3, i % 3]
    sp = part(Ss_["surf_points"], so, i); cp = part(Ss_["surf_cp"], so, i)
    sc = depth_scatter(ax, sp[:, [0, 2]], sp[:, 1], cp, s=1.2, cmap=DIVERGING, norm=norm); map_axes(ax)
    ax.set_xlim(*xlim); ax.set_ylim(*zlim)
    ax.set_title(f"{c['family']} {c['case']}\nL {c['length']:.2f} m, W {c['width']:.2f} m, H {c['height']:.2f} m", fontsize=7.8)
    if i == 0:
        x0 = c["bbox"][0][0]; z0 = c["bbox"][1][2] + 0.35
        ax.annotate("", xy=(x0 + 1.2, z0), xytext=(x0, z0), arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=INK, lw=1.6))
        ax.text(x0 + 1.35, z0, f"$\\hat g_1$, {np.linalg.norm(c['U_inf']):.0f} m/s", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=7.5, color=INK2)
    if i % 3 == 0: ax.set_ylabel("z [m]")
    if i // 3 == 1: ax.set_xlabel("x [m]")
cb = fig.colorbar(sc, ax=axes, fraction=0.02, pad=0.01, extend="min"); cb.set_label("$C_p$ [–]"); cb.outline.set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```

**Diversity.** Within a family the geometry varies as on DrivAerML, by parametric morphs of one body; between the two families the rear end changes class, estate against fastback, which is a larger step than any morph. The far-field speed is fixed and lower than DrivAerML's, a Reynolds-number shift that every architecture sees alike since none receives the Reynolds number ($K = 1$, $S = 0$). The set therefore offers two axes the car set does not: a held-out geometry class and a covariate shift in regime, both as zero-shot targets for a DrivAerML checkpoint.

### Files, conversion and normalization {#sec-data-shift-suv}

**Sport-utility bodies in two rear-end families, estate and fastback,
read with DrivAerML's transform pipeline frozen so that a DrivAerML
checkpoint can be evaluated on them unchanged.** The curated manifest
separates the estate family (794 / 99 / 100 cases for training /
validation / test) from the fastback family (796 / 99 / 99); the frozen
inventory with the split hashes and the exclusion policy is
`results/shift_suv_full_dataset_inventory_2026-07-29/inventory.json`.
The recipe reads each run's `domain.pdmsh` boundary tensordict
(`run_*/domain.pdmsh/_tensordict/boundaries/vehicle`) under the family
subdirectory, and merges the case's `U_inf`, `p_inf`, `rho_inf`, `nu`,
`L_ref`. The sample fastback in @tbl-data-samples has 5.0 million surface
cells.

- **What is the same as DrivAerML.** `L_ref` is 5.0 m in both datasets,
  so the nondimensional coordinates are on the same scale; the same
  nondimensionalization, the same `wss` standard deviation and the same
  subsampling are applied; the fields `pressure_average` and
  `wall_shear_stress_average` are the time-averaged analogues of
  DrivAerML's `pMeanTrim` and `wallShearStressMeanTrim` (SI units verified
  against the release's `units.json`).
- **What differs, and how it is handled.** SHIFT-SUV stores absolute
  pressure with `p_inf` = 101,325 Pa where DrivAerML stores gauge pressure
  with `p_inf` = 0. The shared transform $(p - p_\infty) / q_\infty$ gives
  a proper pressure coefficient for both, with no correction. The
  far-field speed is 30.0 m/s against DrivAerML's 38.89, a Reynolds number
  about 1.3 times lower. Every model receives the unit direction only and
  none receives the Reynolds number, so this is a covariate shift
  identical for every architecture. It is reported alongside the
  geometry-family shift rather than corrected.
- **Role.** The fastback family is held out from every model in the book
  and is the zero-shot target of the cross-family transfer measurements
  (@sec-limits-transfer); the estate training split is a training source
  only where a two-family model is compared.
- **License.** As for DrivAerML, not restated here.

## What is measured {#sec-shift-suv-measured}

**The Surface task of @sec-surface, with the fastback family held out from every model in the book as a zero-shot target and the estate family a training source only where a two-family model is compared.** The instrument is surface pressure and wall shear on the family's validation cases at 200,000 cells, float32, as on DrivAerML. Cross-family transfer is one of the six generalization axes of @sec-problem and is unmeasured for ISLA: no ISLA lane exists on this dataset at any budget, and the earlier finding that cross-family error is governed by the diversity of the training data is a mechanism finding on the architectures tested, not a ranking (@sec-limits-transfer).

## The standing {#sec-shift-suv-standing}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-shift-suv-protocols

protocol_table("shift_suv_surface.json", "tbl-shift-suv-protocols", "Shift-SUV, the Surface task")
```

## What this dataset does not say {#sec-shift-suv-limits}

**Nothing yet about ISLA.** Until the three architectures are trained and scored on it under the protocol, this dataset is a description of a target and not evidence for or against any architecture. When it is scored, a within-family standing says what a second car family says about in-distribution accuracy, and a zero-shot evaluation of DrivAerML checkpoints on the fastback family is the cross-family measurement of @sec-limits-transfer; neither replaces the other.
